title: Module release gates and canary upgrade playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook for releasing Terraform modules used in Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), publishing them to our internal module registry, and rolling upgrades using a canary + phased strategy. The goal is to reduce surprise breakages for customers and internal teams while keeping release cadence manageable.

Audience:
- Module authors (infra and private-deployments eng)
- Solutions Eng / Professional Services (who onboard customers)
- SRE / Platform engineers who operate upgrade rollouts

Scope:
Covers module versioning conventions, automated gating checks, publish steps to the internal registry, a canary upgrade plan for on-prem deployments, and a checklist for handling breaking changes and migrations. Does NOT include code-level implementation details for each module; those live in the module repos.

High-level principles (short):
- Treat the module registry as the contract surface. Consumers should be able to rely on minor/patch upgrades not changing resource semantics.
- Explicitly gate breaking changes: require approval, migration plan, and a deprecation window.
- Use automated tests (unit, acceptance, contract) and CI gates before publishing to registry.
- Canary real customers or internal testbeds before wide rollout.

Versioning policy (semver-based but adapted):
- We use semver: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
- PATCH: bug fixes, documentation, non-behavioral changes. Safe to auto-publish with green CI.
- MINOR: adds new optional inputs/outputs, new resources that are additive and non-breaking. Require contract tests and partner verification if module is widely used.
- MAJOR: any change that removes or renames inputs/outputs, renames resources, or changes behavior requiring state migration. Must follow breaking-change process (see below).

Compatibility gates (CI checks to pass before registry publish):
1) Lint and fmt (tflint, terraform fmt)
2) Module unit tests (kitchen/terratest as implemented for module)
3) Contract tests: a set of minimal consumer configs exercised in CI that validate key inputs/outputs remain stable for minor/patch
4) Provider compatibility tests: run with our supported provider versions matrix (AWS/GCP/Azure versions we support)
5) Static analysis for potential resource name changes (heuristic script)
6) Changelog present and linked PR description

Publish workflow (internal registry):
- Branch: feature/<short-desc>
- PR checklist: include migration notes if needed, update examples, update docs site snippet
- On PR merge to main: CI builds module artifact, runs above gates; if green then create release commit that bumps version in versions.tf or module metadata file
- Tag release: vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (annotated tag) and push tag
- Registry publish step: CI artifacts uploader posts to internal Terraform Registry API with signed artifact and checksums
- Post-publish: create release notes page and mail/slack announcement to #private-deployments and solutions-eng.

Release metadata (required):
- release_version (string)
- changelog_summary (1-3 bullets)
- breaking_changes: yes/no + summary (if yes, link to migration playbook)
- ci_build_id and artifact checksum

Canary upgrade plan (on-prem / VPC customers):
1) Canary targets: choose 1–3 internal test tenants or non-critical customers who have an active support relationship and can accept early upgrades. Prefer customers with small infra footprint and scheduled maintenance windows.
2) Canary window: schedule a 24–72 hour observation window depending on risk level.
3) Preflight: verify current metrics baseline (deploy success rate, apply time, error rate, infra cost estimate). Snapshot terraform state for each target.
4) Apply strategy: apply module bump in a dedicated feature branch locally or via automated runbooks; use job-run tags to identify canary runs.
5) Telemetry checks (automated): plan must define queries and thresholds for immediate rollback, e.g. failed apply rate > 10% or resource drift > X, long-running applies > 2x baseline, endpoint failures increase by > 5%
6) Manual validation: Solutions eng to verify app smoke tests, basic functionality, and any customer-specific assertions
7) Decision point: if canary OK, promote to phased rollout; if not OK, trigger rollback plan and root cause investigation.

Phased rollout (post-canary):
- Phase 1: 10% of customers (by footprint) or non-critical tenants. Monitor for 48 hours.
- Phase 2: 50% of customers. Monitor additional 72 hours.
- Phase 3: All remaining customers.
Notes: timing adjusted based on severity and customer SLAs. Communication must be coordinated with Solutions Eng and CSMs.

Rollback plan (if apply fails or regression found):
- If failure occurs during canary: immediate terraform rollback using saved plan or previous module version, apply to affected states. Use state snapshots to revert state changes if necessary.
- If failure discovered post-apply but within observation window: open emergency migration PR to revert module bump, and coordinate controlled rollback windows per customer.
- Escalation: page on-call infra lead + module author + customer success lead.

Breaking-change checklist (required for MAJOR release):
- [ ] Document explicit list of breaking changes and affected resources/inputs/outputs
- [ ] Provide migration scripts (terraform state mv, state replace-provider, or helper modules)
- [ ] Provide a minimal reproducible example of migration in examples/migration/ folder
- [ ] Run migration with internal test tenants and confirm end-to-end success
- [ ] Provide deprecation timeline (e.g., old module support window: 90 days)
- [ ] Update release notes with step-by-step rollback and contact points
- [ ] Obtain approvals from: solutions-eng, sre, private-deployments lead, legal/compliance if applicable
- [ ] Add deprecation warnings to examples and docs (and emit warnings in CI if possible)

Terraform-specific guidance and gotchas:
- State renames: if a resource logical name must change, prefer introducing new resource and deprecating the old resource instead of renaming in-place. When unavoidable, provide exact terraform state mv commands and validate them in a sandbox state first.
- Inputs/outputs: treat outputs as part of the contract. Avoid renaming or changing types without MAJOR bump. For optional inputs that become required, provide a migration path and defaults where safe.
- Provider pinning: modules must declare a provider version range compatible with our supported matrix. Breaking provider upgrades should be handled separately and coordinated across modules.
- Examples: publish a set of example consumer configs for each module version in the examples/ folder; examples must include pinned provider versions and a note about state migration if applicable.

Release PR template (excerpt to include in module repos):
- Short summary of change
- Version bump: MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH
- Changelog bullets
- Tests run and results (links to CI)
- Breaking change? yes/no. If yes, migration plan link and deprecation schedule.
- Requested approvers: @solutions-eng, @sre, @private-deployments

Notifications and coordination:
- Once published: post in #private-deployments with release summary and link to registry and changelog
- If breaking change: send targeted email to Solutions Eng and any customers who declared interest in early upgrades.
- Update internal dashboard listing modules with last release date, version, and known breaking changes.

Operational runbooks for SRE and Solutions Eng (short pointers):
- How to identify an impacted customer: run the module-usage script (scripts/module-usage.sh) that enumerates states using the module version
- How to perform a rollback: reference the rollback playbook with commands and required approvals
- Who to call: on-call infra lead, module author, solutions-eng contact, CSM assigned to customer

Changelog format (recommended):
- Header: Version + date + author
- Sections: Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed / Security
- Each item should link to PR or Jira ticket

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we require signed module artifacts for all MAJOR releases? (security tradeoffs and UX)
- Automate notification to customers who reference a module in their state (privacy considerations)
- Consider a "compatibility badge" in the registry UI showing which provider versions and platform versions the module was validated against
- Build a migration test harness that can run stateful migration tests on a fresh sandbox infra for each module release

Appendix: quick commands and examples
- Bump version locally: sed -i 's/version = \"0.1.2\"/version = \"0.2.0\"/' metadata.tf  # example
- Tagging: git tag -a v0.2.0 -m "module release v0.2.0" && git push origin v0.2.0
- State mv example: terraform state mv module.old_resource.aws_instance.example module.new_resource.aws_instance.example
- Publish (CI): ./ci/publish_module.sh --artifact build/module-v0.2.0.tgz --registry internal-registry.redwood.ai

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short and link to per-module playbooks for specifics
- Coordinate with product-hosted-api team for any registry UI changes needed
- Run a dry-run with the enterprise demo tenant before first canary

End of draft.
